solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Study poetry, then discuss

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A student reads poems and then talks them over.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, the same as to discuss something.

clue.text: Happy former PM, having lost weight

indicators.note: having lost tells us a piece is taken away from the prime minister's name

parts.note: William Gladstone was a Victorian British prime minister
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister is cheerful after slimming down.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is a British unit of body weight (14 lb), so losing it from the PM's surname is the joke of a slimmer leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and happy are straightforward synonyms for feeling pleased.

clue.text: Rare shock Conservative getting in

indicators.note: getting in means one piece enters another, here the party letter entering the fright

parts.note: a scare is a fright or shock

explanation.surface: An unusual upset as a Conservative wins an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce and rare both describe something seldom found.

clue.text: Glove relative left in pocket

indicators.note: in places the relative and the side letter within the verb for pocketing

parts.note: to pocket money is to get or gain it
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone's relative has left a glove in their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a stout glove, often with a long flared cuff.

clue.text: Special item

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means special or specific
a noun for a single detail or item

explanation.definitionFit: Particular is both an adjective meaning special and a noun meaning an individual item or detail.

clue.text: Plant disease in most of Britain

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the name for Britain is dropped

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang for Britain or home

explanation.surface: A crop disease has spread over most of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY is soldiers' slang for Britain, from Hindustani; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a disease of plants causing withering, as in potato blight.

clue.text: Takes in top paper

parts.note: to take someone in is to fool them
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the best newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a size of writing paper, traditionally about 13 by 16 inches.

clue.text: Amusing imitation in bar in Settle?

indicators.note: the second in places the stick inside the verb for settling up

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A comic impression performed in a pub in the Yorkshire town of Settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire, whose capital letter disguises the verb; the first 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a comic imitation of a style or work.

clue.text: A farmer finally fit, fit for ploughing

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the farmer

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A farmer has at last recovered and can get back to his fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' appears twice: the first is the wordplay piece, the second begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is suitable for ploughing and growing crops.

clue.text: Eager singer to return

indicators.note: to return says the word for the singer is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic singer is keen to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager.

clue.text: Champing at the bit, gunners round republic

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a ring is a round shape
Togo is a West African republic

explanation.surface: Artillerymen surround a republic, eager for action.
explanation.definitionFit: Champing at the bit is an idiom for being impatient to start, as is raring to go.

clue.text: Civilised ancient city's destruction

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
bane means ruin or destruction

explanation.surface: The sacking of a cultured ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbane person is suave and refined, that is civilised in manner.

clue.text: Regulate trade abroad importing cars

indicators.note: importing means the anagrammed word takes the cars inside it
abroad signals the letters of trade are scattered

parts.note: Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: Controlling overseas commerce by bringing in vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like part of the trade picture but signals the anagram, giving ADTER; 'importing' then takes the cars inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or regulate affairs.

clue.text: Requiring careful handling, domestic pet in food store close to garage

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
a cat is a domestic pet

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of garage

explanation.surface: A house cat kept in a food shop beside a garage needs gentle treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' suggests a container, but here it is only a link word in the surface; the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate matter or object needs to be treated with care.

clue.text: Antagonism shown by heartless adversary carrying it

indicators.note: carrying means the shortened foe holds the next word within it
heartless says the middle letter of the word for adversary goes

parts.note: an enemy is an adversary
it is taken as written

explanation.surface: Hostility displayed by an opponent bearing a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central E of ENEMY to leave ENMY, which then carries IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or antagonism between foes.

clue.text: Charm wild animals after spot of training

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the single letter
a spot of training means just its first letter
wild signals the letters of animals run riot

explanation.surface: Lucky charms for wild beasts after a little schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck, a charm.

clue.text: Showing little interest, stable about foremost of thoroughbreds

indicators.note: about means one word wraps round the other letter

parts.note: solid means stable or firm

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of thoroughbreds

explanation.surface: A racing stable is unmoved by its best horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive and shows little emotion or interest.

clue.text: Avoid fish and fowl

parts.note: to duck is to dodge or avoid
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Dodge the fish and the poultry at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A duckling is a young duck, a kind of fowl.

clue.text: Having little energy in very pleasant Italian city

indicators.note: in puts the small letter into the run formed by the two other words

parts.note: nice means pleasant
E is the symbol for energy, a little of it being one letter

explanation.surface: Feeling tired in a lovely Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the famous canal city of northern Italy.

clue.text: Distressed Hellenic fabric

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Worn Greek cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a velvety tufted fabric or yarn.

clue.text: Home in centre? Middle of nowhere!

parts.note: the heart is the centre of something

indicators.note: Middle of picks the central letter of nowhere

explanation.surface: Being at home in the city centre, or in the middle of nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearth stands for home, the fireside being the centre of the house.

clue.text: Extremely tough breed in ancient land

indicators.note: Extremely picks the letters at the extremities of tough

parts.note: a race is a breed or stock

explanation.surface: A hardy breed of people living in an old country.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of the Balkans north of the Aegean.

clue.text: Evil trap set up for game

indicators.note: set up in a down clue says the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sin is wickedness or evil
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A wicked snare laid for game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SIN+NET into TENNIS, read upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net.

clue.text: Crowd sitting for impromptu jazz concert

parts.note: to jam is to crowd or cram together
a session is a sitting, as of a court

explanation.surface: A packed audience sits for an improvised jazz gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam session is an informal gathering where musicians improvise together.

clue.text: Completely book first social event

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of book and puts it at the front

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Reserve tickets in full for the opening party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering for dancing.

clue.text: Poet's unfinished copy

indicators.note: unfinished says the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A poet's work left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn a disc is to copy data onto it.

clue.text: Two articles about a third patron goddess

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: about turns the third article round

parts.note: a third article is an, the other form of the indefinite one

explanation.surface: A pair of essays concerning a third about a guardian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third' means a third article, the indefinite form used before vowels; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom and patron of Athens.

clue.text: Settler, one wearing strange garment

indicators.note: wearing means the shuffled clothing goes round the numeral letter
strange signals the letters of garment are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newcomer stands out in odd clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns GARMENT into EMGRANT, which wears I.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves their country to settle in another.
